title: Sensitivity analysis for REDD+ carbon accounting
text: REDD+ emission reduction estimate combines many uncertain inputs: areas land use change (activity data, AD), carbon stocks land use, carbon fraction, degradation ratios (together emission factors, EF). Uncertainty analysis (see fct_arithmetic_mean2()) tells uncertain result . Sensitivity analysis answers complementary question: inputs responsible uncertainty? tells country invest next measurement campaign — improving input drives variance cheapest way shrink confidence interval reported emission reduction.

title: Sensitivity analysis for REDD+ carbon accounting
text: land use transition, emissions activity data times emission factor: E=AD×EF×4412,EF=Cinitial−Cfinal E \;=\; AD \times EF \times \tfrac{44}{12}, \qquad EF = C_\text{initial} - C_\text{final} carbon stock CC built carbon pools (optionally carbon fraction , degraded land, degradation ratio applied intact stock). Reference monitoring emission levels period aggregates transitions, emission reduction difference: ER=EREF−EMON. ER = E_\text{REF} - E_\text{MON}. degraded land use reuses intact carbon stock, global carbon fraction shared across land uses, inputs feed several parts model . correct sensitivity analysis must respect shared inputs.

title: Sensitivity analysis for REDD+ carbon accounting
text: reference framework global sensitivity analysis variance-based (Sobol) decomposition (Saltelli et al. 2008). output YY function independent inputs X1,…,XkX_1,\dots,X_k, variance decomposes contributions input interactions: Var⁡(Y)=∑iVi+∑<jVij+… \operatorname{Var}(Y) = \sum_i V_i + \sum_{<j} V_{ij} + \dots Two indices summarise : first-order index Si=Vi/Var⁡(Y)S_i = V_i / \operatorname{Var}(Y), share variance explained XiX_ialone; total index STiS_{T_i}, also includes every interaction involving XiX_i. Sobol indices usually estimated Monte Carlo Saltelli sampling, cost N(k+2)N\,(k+2) model runs. general approach captures interactions, stochastic comparatively expensive.

title: Sensitivity analysis for REDD+ carbon accounting
text: REDD+ emission model sum products (AD × EF), close linear input uncertainty range. model first-order Sobol indices can obtained analytically first-order (delta-method) expansion. independent inputs, Var⁡(Y)≈∑(∂Y∂Xi)2σi2,Si≈(∂Y/∂Xi)2σi2Var⁡(Y). \operatorname{Var}(Y) \;\approx\; \sum_i \Big(\tfrac{\partial Y}{\partial X_i}\Big)^2 \sigma_i^2, \qquad S_i \;\approx\; \frac{\big(\partial Y/\partial X_i\big)^2 \sigma_i^2}{\operatorname{Var}(Y)} . fct_sensitivity2() computes partial derivatives numerically independent inputs used Monte Carlo simulation (carbon pools namespaced land use, carbon fraction, degradation ratios per-transition activity data), shared inputs propagate consistently — perturbing forest’s biomass changes intact stock degraded stock derived . per-input contributions summed REDD+-meaningful input groups: Activity data — transition areas, Carbon stock — carbon pools land use, Carbon fraction — biomass--carbon conversion, Degradation ratio — ratios defining degraded stocks. deterministic, essentially free compute, consistent IPCC Tier 1 uncertainty already reported package. limitation , first-order, resolve interaction terms; interactions expected large, full Sobol analysis appropriate alternative (sketched end article).

title: Calculate emissions and IPCC Tier 1 uncertainty from arithmetic means — fct_arithmetic_mean2
text: Analytical counterpart fct_arithmetic_mean(). Instead Monte Carlo simulations, activity data emission factors aggregated deterministically uncertainty propagated IPCC Tier 1 (first-order error propagation) rules: relative uncertainties combine quadrature products absolute standard errors combine quadrature sums / differences. propagation done numerically independent input variables (carbon pool values, carbon fraction, degradation ratios activity data), correlations introduced shared inputs (e.g. degraded land use reuses intact carbon stock, global carbon fraction) handled consistently. result reports, reference / monitoring emission level emission reduction, mean, standard error, half-width uncertainty \(U\% = z \cdot se / |mean| \cdot 100\), \(z\) two-sided normal quantile setup$conf_level.
